$comment: Licence policy for every package in package-lock.json. Read by
scripts/check-licenses.mjs; the supply-chain CI job runs it. See that
`allowed` holds only licences that are fine for a package that SHIPS:
esbuild inlines some devDependencies into the bundles (NOTICE lists
them), and npm's dev flag cannot tell those from build tools. A package
under any other licence needs an entry in `exceptions`, and its `why` is
the argument that it never reaches a bundle.
An exception is keyed on the package name and its lockfile licence string
together. If the licence changes, or the package leaves the tree, the gate
fails until the entry is re-reasoned or deleted.
Written 2026-09-29 (12q) against 902 lockfile packages: 745 MIT, and every
`OR` expression in the tree has an allowed branch.

exceptions.why: Microsoft's own licence terms for its VSIX signing tool, pulled in by @vscode/vsce and used only at packaging time. Never bundled.
